<reason>PRO built a coherent case (severity physics, 24/7 coverage, armed-encounter externalities) and clearly held the stronger ground on the externality prong, especially by noting CON's reform list concedes structural harms in stops. But CON kept the motion's conjunction in view and did more damage on the safety prong: it forced PRO to concede cameras interrupt no lethal behavior, exposed the point-to-point pivot as a retreat, answered both pressure questions directly with A1/A2 (targeted weekend/high-crash deployment, seatbelt enforcement example), and then landed the "whose speed does a camera actually lower" outlier argument. PRO's second rebuttal and closing never engaged that argument, instead repeating the severity frame and twice claiming CON "never answered" points CON had in fact addressed (once prematurely, before CON's turn). PRO's clipped opening and recap-heavy closing add small execution costs. CON progressed the clash; PRO restated it.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's A4.4–A4.6 turn on PRO's severity pivot—"whose speed does a camera lower? The sober, attentive driver... PRO's mechanism works best on the drivers least likely to die"—directly attacked PRO's fallback for the safety prong, and PRO's closing left it unanswered, letting CON crystallize it as "fatalities live in the outliers."</best_rebuttal>
